title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and claim your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information. They may ask for your Medicare number or Social Security number.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to confirm your information or your coverage will be canceled. Please give us your Medicare number now."
red_flags: Caller says your benefits will be canceled immediately
Asks for your Medicare or Social Security number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer warning of a virus and urges you to call a phone number for help. Scammers pretend to be from Microsoft or another tech company and try to get remote access to your computer or ask for payment.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up says your computer is infected
Asks you to call a phone number right away
Wants remote access to your computer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; if you’re worried, contact a trusted local computer repair shop.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money fast. They may ask you to send cash or gift cards for bail or an emergency.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in trouble and need money for bail. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad. Can you send $2,000 right away?"
red_flags: Caller claims to be a relative in trouble
Wants money sent urgently, often by wire or gift card
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check if the story is true.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text message saying there’s a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link to fix it. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your information.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to update your address: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to a website you don’t recognize
Requests for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Don’t click the link; check your orders directly with the delivery company if you’re expecting a package.

title: Social Security Suspension Email
how_it_works: You receive an email saying your Social Security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity. The email urges you to call a number or click a link to fix the problem.
example_message: "Your Social Security number has been suspended. Call us immediately at 1-888-XXX-XXXX to reactivate your account."
red_flags: Email says your Social Security number is suspended
Asks you to call or click a link
what_to_do: Do not respond; contact the Social Security Administration directly at their official number if you have concerns.
